newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt announces new meat authority.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt announces new meat authority.

text.p: The Australian government said on Tuesday a single meat corporation with one board and separate operational units would replace the red meat industry's three main statutory authorities.

"A producer owned and funded company will be established to replace the Australian Meat and Livestock Corporation, and the Meat Research Corporation," Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said in a statement.
"The Meat Industry Council would be wound-up," Anderson said.
Under the new structure, which will start immediately, separate operating units will be responsible for jointly funded research and development, food safety and quality, he said.
There will also be separately managed operating units for beef and sheepmeat marketing and promotion.
Separate and independent annual reviews will be carried out to monitor the body's performance.
"Meat processors and livestock exporters will establish separate voluntarily funded companies and will interact with the producer company through willing partnership arrangements," Anderson said.
He cautioned that levies would be re-imposed if insufficient funds were raised to meet agreed activities with producers.
A memorandum of understanding between industry sectors and the government would ensure co-operation in the interest of Australia's red meat industry, he said.
Peak industry councils would be invited as a non-executive Red Meat Advisory Council to advise Anderson on policy and the performance of the new body, which is yet to be named.
These changes follow a major government review of the red meat industry which presented the adopted structure as a minority recommendation.
The majority recommendation of the Meat and Livestock Industry Reform task force was for the splitting of the main industry body, the Australian Meat and Livestock Corp, into two separate entities.
